1.2: 1.2 A man appeared coming from the camp of Saul, etc. RABANUS. The Hebrews say this was a son of Doeg. For Amalekite and Edomite are one, because the firstborn son of Esau was Eliphaz, and his son Amalek. He had the diadem and bracelet entrusted by his father.
1.15: 1.15 Approaching, etc. Everyone who plots evil against his neighbor, or rejoices at his destruction, deserves from the supreme judge the punishment of just retribution. For 'he who digs a pit falls into it' (Proverbs 26). And, 'The mouth that lies kills the soul' (Wisdom 1): and this man lied that he had killed Saul.
1.18: 1.18 Sons. The sons of Judah, sons of confession, whom the true David wishes to be fortified with the bow of Scripture, lest through ignorance they succumb in the sight of the demons. Bow. RABANUS, in the Book of Kings. Because the Philistines are archers, by which art they had slain Saul, he wishes them to learn the same art of war, or he commanded that the kings of Judah be taught strength, that is, that they be strong and intent in the fear of the Lord, lest they perish like Saul. In the book. RABANUS, as above. It is read, or, it is written. They affirm this book is found nowhere, like the book of the wars of the Lord, etc., up to how Saul, departing from the fear of the Lord, perished through obedience. Consider, Israel. THE SAME. You who remained, for what fault they were slain, and take care lest you too perish in their crime.
1.20: 1.20 Gath. A winepress, namely Jerusalem, which killed the prophets (Matthew 23), to which the death of the Lord and of the apostles was a derision, and on this account the true David commanded that his passion not be announced to them.
1.21: 1.21 Mountains of Gilboa, etc. THE SAME. Others, lofty, because, namely, O Saul, your disobedience was reckoned as idolatry on the heights, because the crime of idolatry is to refuse to submit. The mountains of Gilboa were most fertile before the curse, which they say to this day lie under the curse, and they testify that it never rains there. King and prophet David, who did not return evils to persecutors, when Saul and Jonathan had fallen in battle, in his lament cursed the mountains of Gilboa: 'Ye mountains of Gilboa, let no dew,' etc., up to and the divine power fulfilled the sentence of the one cursing. Thus for the spectacle of the royal death the elements paid the penalty. RABANUS. What did the mountains do wrong? etc., up to who with iniquity demanding had deserved to receive among themselves the death of the king.
1.22: 1.22 From the blood of the slain. Blood and fat give strength to the body; so they gave strength to the subjected, by whom Saul and Jonathan were slain as though not by rustics. Or thus Saul was rejected by God, and basely slain by the uncircumcised, as though he had not been anointed with oil, on account of the blood of the slain, namely the eighty-five priests who burned fat to the Lord, whom Saul commanded to be killed though innocent. Arrow. He signifies that Jonathan and Saul were warlike and most valiant, and praises in them beauty of form and constancy of mind. RABANUS. Allegorically. The pious prophet David figuratively mourns Saul and Jonathan, etc., up to lest again shamefully overcome, they give joy to the enemies.
2.1: 2.1 After this. RABANUS. The going up of David with two wives into Hebron signifies the calling together of the two peoples into the Catholic Church. For Hebron is interpreted 'marriage.' But the Church alone is the bride of the heavenly king. There David led each man with his household, because each of the faithful is called into that society by the preaching of the Gospel, where there is no distinction of Jew and Greek.
2.4: 2.4 And they came. THE SAME. Because, while the proud and contemptuous spurn the grace of God, the elect, by the fame of preaching and zeal for virtues, confess that Christ is king among his people, to whom all power is given in heaven and on earth.
2.5: 2.5 And he said. THE SAME. It greatly pleases our Redeemer, who condemns and consigns to oblivion the works of the wicked who are dead in sins, nor imitates what displeases the Lord, but remembers to do what he commanded.
2.8: 2.8 Ishbosheth. THE SAME. Who is interpreted 'son of confusion,' with the help of Abner, who is interpreted 'lamp of the father,' reigned over all Israel, and only the house of Judah followed David, because to those alone who believe and truly confess, following Christ, while in the rest the error of confusion reigned, at the instigation of the devil who transforms himself into an angel of light (2 Corinthians 11). He led around. In the Hebrew it is said: He led him over to Mahanaim, which is interpreted 'camps'; he led him, namely, across the Jordan, and set him up as king in the camps.
2.11: 2.11 And the time. RABANUS, in the Book of Kings, vol. 2. He rightly said that David reigned seven years and six months in Hebron, etc., up to and it was built seven years before Tanis, a city of Egypt.
2.12: 2.12 Abner went out. RABANUS. Josephus explains this passage thus, etc., up to here Abner pursued, turning aside to neither side.
2.18: 2.18 Now Asahel was a most swift runner, like one of the roes. THE SAME, from Gregory. Asahel signifies those whom vehement fury seizes and leads headlong, etc., up to as though they die without the sword.
2.26: 2.26 Do you not know that despair is dangerous? In the Hebrew it is: Do you not know that the end will be bitter, if you strive to destroy the people?
3.1: 3.1 Now there was. RABANUS, in the Book of Kings. The house of David is the heavenly Jerusalem, etc., up to and at last, according to his merits, he will be submerged in the depth of the abyss.
3.2: 3.2 And sons were born. The six sons who were born to David in Hebron signify the perfection of the saints, who arise daily from the spiritual marriage of Christ and the Church by the grace of the Holy Spirit.
3.5: 3.5 Of Eglah. RABANUS. This is Michal, who alone is called wife, because David obtained her as his first wife in his youth. She is said to have died in childbirth, whence it is written in what follows: 'Michal the daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death,' because she died in the very childbirth.
3.17: 3.17 The word. THE SAME. Abner exhorts all Israel, etc., up to and everywhere persecuted the faith of Christ.
3.29: 3.29 A flux of seed. According to the letter he seems to imprecate an outflow of lust, the plague of leprosy, effeminacy, that the enemy lie under the sword, begging. Holding the spindle. AUGUSTINE. By circumlocution of words are noted those who strive to defend their deceit. Falling. 'He who strikes with the sword shall perish by the sword' (Matthew 26). Heretics pierce with the sword of the mouth, first themselves pierced through by the sword of impiety.
3.39: 3.39 Delicate. The ancients called delicate things consecrated to the gods, which we now call dedicated.
4.2: 4.2 And two men. RABANUS, in the Book of Kings, vol. 2. These two men were captains in the army of Ishbosheth, and, Abner being dead, as the Hebrews relate, they consulted with Mephibosheth to kill Ishbosheth and set him up as king. But Mephibosheth betrayed the plan; therefore he is introduced thus: 'He was the son of Jonathan, lame in his feet.' They, terrified by fear, fled to Gittaim, and were there until that time when, returning from there, they entered the house of Ishbosheth. And the doorkeeper. THE SAME. The doorkeeper cleans wheat, etc., up to lest enemies penetrate through the hole of a neglected thought.
5.1: 5.1 And they came. RABANUS. So all nations come to Christ, and as though flattering say: 'We are your bone and your flesh': since in him they love and venerate the incarnation which he took from our nature in the womb of the virgin.
5.3: 5.3 The elders. THE SAME. The prophets and apostles run together to Christ with equal faith and devotion. And they anointed. THE SAME. David is said to have been anointed twice, and Christ took the principate first among the Jews, afterward among the Gentiles.
5.4: 5.4 And forty. THE SAME. It is asked why forty years and six months are not counted in the sum? etc., up to which consists of four tens, signifies the perfection of times and things.
5.5: 5.5 In Jerusalem. The Hebrews relate that Shem the son of Noah, whom they say is Melchizedek, founded Salem. The Jebusites held it afterward, from whom it received the name Jebus. Hence Jerusalem, as though Jebus Salem, afterward by Solomon Hierosolyma, as though Hierosolomonia, which afterward was called Aelia by Aelius Hadrian.
5.6: 5.6 The blind and the lame. Who suffice against you. They said this trusting in their walls. Or thus: you will not enter unless you remove us, whom you think unarmed like the blind and the lame, and think you triumph.
5.7: 5.7 But David took. RABANUS. As Josephus says, etc., up to which is rightly called the citadel of Sion, that is, of watching, so that it is rightly said of it: 'His place is made in peace,' etc. (Psalm 75). David took the citadel of Sion, the blind and the lame who hate the soul of David having first been removed. So the Lord acquired primacy in the Church of the Gentiles, his Scribes and Pharisees having been rejected, who, blind and lame, hated the soul of Christ, that is, tried to take away his life.
5.8: 5.8 Of the roofs. That is, of the rulers. He calls pipes the water conduits made of lead or by a rule, through which water went over the wall through the whole city. Pipes. They figure false knowledge or the dogmas of heretics, which the Lord destroys through Joab, that is, the preachers. The Jebusite trampling: this is the Gentile world, which before the faith trampled the precepts of God. Likewise the Jebusite trodden down, because the devil is trodden down by the Lord, and is subjected to be trodden down under Joab.
5.9: 5.9 And he built. From the place so called, understand 'the wall'; and inside, understand 'another wall,' that is, he fortified the city with a double wall.
5.11: 5.11 Hiram also sent. Hiram, living on high, this is the Gentile world exalted in Christ; he sends messengers to David, that is, teachers to Christ, and through them cedar wood, that is, incorrupt and strong men; and craftsmen, that is, those by whose art minds are incorrupt, and like stones squared by the four virtues, so the house of David, that is, the Church of Christ, is built, and it is known that God has confirmed our David king over Israel, that is, those seeing God. RABANUS. The churches of heretics who boast of remaining under the title of the Christian name. But because they follow Christ for carnal gains, they are called not wives but concubines. Now, however, if kings have several wives or concubines, it is a sin: because the figures have passed away, for which this was at one time venial.
5.13: 5.13 And were born. If Christ is signified by David, not undeservedly by his sons are understood Christians, who are from the Jews and the nations, to whom the interpretations of the names agree: Shammua, boldness; Shobab, converting; Ibhar, he chose; Elishua, salvation of my God; Nepheg, applying to the mouth; Japhia, he enlightens or shows; Elishama, my God hearing; Eliada, my God knows; Eliphelet, my God saving.
5.20: 5.20 Baal-perazim. It is interpreted 'division of enemies.' The place can be so called because the Philistines left their idols in the place where they were divided.
5.23: 5.23 Of the pear trees. In the Hebrew, of the weeping ones, that is, of idols, where namely were the idols in which they trusted, which are called weeping ones, because they are worthy of weeping, and lead their worshippers to weeping and misery. At the top. RABANUS. 'Pyrus' is said from the Greek, which is 'fire.' The pear trees are the saints: the top, the sublimity of their life; in which, the Holy Spirit blowing, the sound of preaching thundered. Which is of one advancing, that is, the gift of one coming in the flesh, at the top of the pear trees, that is, above the height of the saints, while this sound is heard by our David, the intelligible Philistines are overcome.
6.1: 6.1 He gathered. RABANUS, from Eucherius. David Christ, etc., up to who coming down from Judea taught the brethren: 'Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved' (Acts 15).
6.2: 6.2 Of him who sits. Over the ark was a tablet which two cherubim covered with their wings, between whom the Lord appeared and spoke. RABANUS, from Gregory. In the history of King and prophet David, in which he is said to have brought up the ark of God, humility is shown approved, pride condemned, and rashness avenged. For David, who was not ashamed to dance humbly before the ark, soon deserved to receive the promise of the Son of God to be born of his stock, and the wife who despised his humility paid the penalty of perpetual barrenness. The priest also who rashly touched the ark purged the guilt of his daring by an untimely death. Here it is to be considered how much he offends who approaches the body of the Lord guilty, if that man is punished with death who handled the ark, the figure of the Lord's body, with less veneration than he ought. GREGORY, Moralia, book V, chap. 10. Often because they cannot understand, etc., up to that they might not judge the deeds or words of better men as if weak.
6.7: 6.7 Who died. RABANUS, from Eucherius. The priest being dead, he did not dare to turn aside the ark, etc., up to Water: the Gittite people can be so called, who says, 'But far be it from me to glory, save in the cross of the Lord' (Galatians 6).
6.11: 6.11 Three months. THE SAME. By which, namely, faith, hope and charity are signified, etc., up to and they bear the leadership of the sheep, crowning in the blood of martyrdom. On instruments. That is, bound to the arm, while they are touched by the hands of the bearer. Another kind of instrument is that which is made with water.
6.14: 6.14 In a linen ephod, and David, etc. RABANUS. Not in a pontifical but in a linen garment, for the sake of humility, etc., up to amid the scourges he triumphed.
6.16: 6.16 And when he had entered the ark. THE SAME. With all rejoicing and resounding hymns at the entrance of the heavenly ark, etc., up to because those who receive the word of God only by ear, without the offspring of good work, await the day of perpetual death.
6.20: 6.20 Michal the daughter of Saul coming out to meet David, etc. GREGORY, Moralia, book XXVII, chap. 27. It is pleasing to behold how great gifts of virtues David had received, etc., up to yet he pressed down the neck of his heart with the strong heel of discretion, saying: And I will be humble in my own eyes. Glorious. When David transferred the ark to Jerusalem, he was mocked by Michal. And Christ, when he transferred the New Testament into his Church, was a mockery to the Jews on the cross, appeared naked while, hiding his power from them, he showed the weakness of the flesh as a linen ephod. The handmaids bear the person of the servants of the saints, among whom through the triumph of the cross he was made more glorious: while Michal derides him he appears more glorious to the handmaids, she who in the type of the Synagogue remained barren. And uncovered. Not wholly uncovered, but of the royal garments: and because he was not ashamed to humble himself before the Lord, he soon deserved to receive the promise of the Son of God to be born of his stock.
7.3: 7.3 All that is in your heart, go and do. RABANUS, in the Book of Kings, vol. 3. It is clear that the spirit of prophecy does not always illumine the minds of the prophets. For the Spirit breathes where he will (John 3). Hence Elisha says: 'The Lord has hidden it from me and has not told me' (2 Kings 4). Which God arranges by a dispensation of kindness: because while he gives and withdraws the spirit of prophecy, he lifts the minds of the prophets to a height and keeps them in humility, so that, receiving the spirit, they may find what they are from God, and again, not having the spirit of prophecy, they may know what they are from themselves. GREGORY, Moralia, book VII, chap. 17. One must be clean from vices in himself, etc., up to it is necessary that he be ashamed to instruct the minds of neighbors.
7.5: 7.5 Shall you? RABANUS. Another translation, etc., up to he himself will build me a house.
7.10: 7.10 And I will appoint a place. He describes the time of Solomon, in which the children of Israel had peace on all sides and were not afflicted as in the time of the Judges.
7.16: 7.16 And faithful. RABANUS, from Augustine, City of God, book 17, chap. 8. This is truly said of Christ, etc., up to the place therefore of so peaceful and secure a dwelling is eternal, where there will be the true Israel, that is, seeing God. And he sat before. To sit before the Lord is to confess his benefits in humility. The law of Adam. RABANUS. Namely of man, that he may serve you in simplicity of heart and purity, and that you may do for him according to your mercy, as you have done for me.
7.23: 7.23 Which is. In another land beside the chosen one, for which the Son of God came into the world as into Egypt, to redeem for himself by the exchange of blood an acceptable people, a follower of good works. And the God of that same people we understand as the Lord's man, whom he assumed from Egypt, that is, the world, through the womb of the virgin. From Egypt. The nation and its God, or the nation and its God, the nation of Israel, and its God Moses, of whom: 'I have appointed you the god of Pharaoh' (Exodus 7).
7.27: 7.27 Your servant has found. Nothing is more fleeting than the heart, which is found when it is restrained by discretion.
8.1: 8.1 The bridle. There were five cities of the Philistines which made Israel tributary. David took these for himself and made them tributary, as is read: 'David smote the Philistines, and humbled them, and took Gath and its daughters out of their hand,' etc. (1 Chronicles 18). The bridle. Christ, triumphing over the powers of the air, broke the bridle of error which they had put on the human race.
8.2: 8.2 Making equal. For men living on the earth were not humbled so much that, a line being stretched out, they appeared equal with the ground: but so vile and despised that they were worth no more than the earth which has no men. He put the measuring line for a lot; because a line is customarily used for measuring, according to that: 'And he divided to them the land by lot with a line of distribution' (Psalm 77). It signifies that he divided the regions of the Moabites to whomever he wished as freely as an owner his own fields. RABANUS. It signifies that those whom he wished he could kill, and those whom he wished he could spare. That he made Moab, which is interpreted 'from the father,' and Syria of Damascus and the other regions tributary signifies that Christ holds all nations under his dominion, and presses them, and exacts the tribute of good works. Damascus, a noble city of Phoenicia, is said with the same name as Maseth, the son of Abraham's handmaid, and is interpreted 'cup of blood.' Syria is 'lofty' or 'moist'; for what was first moist with lust, insatiably thirsting for human blood, now cleansed by the baptism of Christ, lofty in progress of virtues, desires the cup of his blood.
8.11: 8.11 King David sanctified. So Christ, of all whom he calls from the nations, makes some like gold, that is, spiritual in sense, some like silver, that is, shining with the brightness of eloquence; others like bronze, sounding in preaching, he sanctifies to the Lord, that they may faithfully serve his tabernacle.
8.13: 8.13 Having slain. JEROME. That in some codices twelve thousand are said to have been slain is a scribal error that has taken root. For in truth David slew eighteen thousand in the valley of the Salt Pits. Joab slew twelve thousand, as is written in the title of Psalm 58. It is signified that Christ, by the strictness of his examination, extinguishes in those who think wrongly of him the folly of immoderate labor.
8.16: 8.16 Over the records. He acted in place of the king, by whose judgment the laws were written. The scribe wrote down by word what came from the king's mouth.
8.17: 8.17 The priests. Priest (sacerdos) as if 'sacred leader' (sacer dux). The sons of David held command in the tribe of Judah. RABANUS. They sat with the king guarding his body, and are interpreted 'killing and giving life,' since according to their judgment the worthy were reserved for life, others were led to death.
9.1: 9.1 And David said, etc. RABANUS, in the Book of Kings, vol. 3. Behold, David was not forgetful of the oath and covenant which he made with Jonathan, etc., up to because they come into the admiration of the people who lately were despised in the world and appear glorious in the Church.
10.1: 10.1 Now it came to pass after this that the king of the children of Ammon died, etc. I will do, etc. JEROME. When David fled from the face of Achish king of Gath, he came to Nahash king of Ammon, who showed him mercy. From Nahash, then, he came to the cave of Adullam, where his father and mother and all his house came to him: from there he came to Moab, and left his father and mother and all his house with him. As for what Achish king of Gath said: 'Shall this man enter my house?', David went from there and fled to the cave of Adullam (1 Samuel 21), 'the house of Nahash' is to be understood. If it is asked why he returned to Achish, whom he had fled before, it is to be understood that the one to whom he returned was the son of him whom he fled. Hence in what follows Achish, with whom David went down to battle, is said to have a son Maoch. For he took this patronymic not from his father but from his mother, who was called Maacah.
10.4: 10.4 So Hanun took the servants of David, and shaved off the beard, etc. RABANUS, from Eucherius. These things signify the war of the devil against the Church. For Hanun, that is, 'their sorrow,' signifies the devil, who is ruler of the Ammonites, that is, of malignant spirits, the people of sorrow and ever placed in distress, who desires to oppress or distress men. Hanun therefore shaves half the beard of David's messengers, when the devil stains the speech or conduct of certain preachers by corrupting it. He cuts the tunics up to the loins, when he reveals before the eyes of men the shameful deeds which he persuades. These must sit in Jericho until the beard grows, lest they be a reproach to others and an anathema to all, that is, until increases of virtues are born in them, and they are held worthy to be presented to their king. But our David does not suffer his soldiers to be unavenged, but, an army gathered, avenges the injury of his own, and not only confounds the adversaries by the victory of his saints but even in the final judgment hands them over to perpetual fires.
11.1: 11.1 And it came to pass at the turn of the year, at the time when, etc. RABANUS, from Jerome. That is, in spring, when the harshness of the cold is driven off and fodder for the beasts of burden is found, etc., up to but they were conquered.
11.2: 11.2 While these things. RABANUS. David sinned gravely, etc., up to who healed so grave a wound of sin by the confession of humility. Bathsheba. ISIDORE. Well of satiety, or the seventh well. The Church is called a well of living water, and to this well the name of the number seven is joined in signification of the Holy Spirit, by reason of Pentecost, on which day the Holy Spirit was sent from heaven. To forty-nine, that is, seven times seven, one is added, because unity is commended. Hence: 'Careful to keep the unity of the spirit in the bond of peace' (Ephesians 4). By the spiritual gift, that is, the sevenfold, the Church has become a well of satiety, because there has been made in her a fountain of water springing up into eternal life, which whoever drinks shall not thirst for ever (John 4). GREGORY. Still weighed down by the burden of corruptible flesh, we cannot so live that no delight of fault can assail us. But it is one thing not to wish to be touched, another to consent. Holy men guard themselves with so much the more watchful circumspection as they disdain to be assailed even transiently by sinister motions, so that if the heart should perhaps desire something unlawful, the eye, restrained by the discipline of the master, refuses to see: for as temptation is often drawn in through the eyes, so sometimes what is conceived within compels the eye to serve it from without. Very often something is looked upon with an innocent mind, but in the very sight the mind is pierced by the sword of concupiscence. David did not look carefully at the wife of Uriah because he had desired her, but rather desired her because he had looked incautiously. By the just examination of retribution, he who uses the outer eye negligently is blinded in the inner eye. Often, however, concupiscence already rules within, and the enticed mind, in the manner of tyranny, demands that the bodily senses serve its uses, and compels the eyes to serve its pleasures, and opens the windows of light to the darkness of blindness. Hence holy men, when they feel themselves assailed by sinister delight, restrain by the discipline of the master the very lights through which the appearance of form enters the mind, lest the sight, panderer to a wicked thought, serve it: for if this is ever neglected to be subtly guarded, the uncleanness of thought passes into action. GREGORY. Often a thing is virtue according to the history, but fault according to the signification; as sometimes fault in the deed, virtue in the writing of prophecy. For who would not detest that David, walking on the roof, desired Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah, whom yet, returning from the battle, he bids go home and wash his feet? Who at once answered saying: 'The ark of God is under skins, and shall I rest in my house?' Whom David received at his own table and gave him feasts by which he was to die. David therefore holds the figure of him of whom it is written: 'He has set his tabernacle in the sun' (Psalm 18). Who orders Bathsheba to be brought to him, that is, to join to himself by spiritual understanding the law of the letter joined to a carnal people. Bathsheba is called 'well of seven,' because through the kinship of the law, by the infusion of special grace, perfect wisdom is ministered to us. Uriah signifies the Jewish people, interpreted 'my light of God': for the Jewish people, which is exalted by the knowledge of the law it has received, glories as in the light of God. But David took his wife from him and joined her to himself, because the Redeemer, appearing strong of hand, while he made known that the law spoke spiritually of himself, by this that they held it according to the letter, showed it estranged from the Jewish people; he joined it to himself, because he declared himself preached through it. Yet he bids Uriah go home and wash his feet, because the incarnate One commands the Jews to return to conscience, and wipe away the filth of works with tears; that they may understand the commandments of the law specially, and after so great a hardness of precepts, finding the fountain of baptism, run to the water after labor. But Uriah, who remembers that the ark of the Lord is under skins, answers that he cannot enter his house. Which is to say: I see the commandments of God in carnal sacrifices, and I do not seek to return to conscience through spiritual understanding. For he says the ark of God is under skins because he understands the precepts of God only by performing the ministry of carnal sacrifice. Yet David calls him, unwilling to return home, to his table, because, though the Jews disdain to return to conscience, Christ nevertheless preaches spiritual things, saying: 'If you believed Moses, you would perhaps believe me also, for he wrote of me' (John 5). For the Jew holds the law, which speaks of his divinity, and disdains to believe. Hence Uriah is also sent to Joab with letters by which he is to be killed, because the Jew carries the law, by whose convicting he is to die. For when, holding to the commandments of the law, he strives to fulfill them, he himself carries the judgment by which he is condemned. What then is more wicked than this deed of David? What cleaner than Uriah? But as to the mystery: what holier than David? What more faithless than Uriah? Because the one through fault of life signifies the innocence of prophecy; and the other through innocence of life expresses fault in prophecy. For the power of sacred speech so narrates things done as to express things to come: thus in the deed it approves the matter, as in the mystery it contradicts. Thus it condemns what was done, that it may persuade that these things be done mystically.
11.15: 11.15 Set Uriah, etc. GREGORY, Moralia, book XXXIII, chap. 10. For this the sins of David and Peter are placed in Scripture, that the fall of the greater be a caution for the lesser, etc., up to by the secret order of dispensation, therefore, from which the iniquity of the devil is permitted to rage, from there the kindness of God is brought to completion, because from there he obeys the nods of supernal grace, from which he exercises the wrath of his will.
12.13: 12.13 And Nathan said to David, etc. RABANUS, from Eucherius. Yet all that was foretold to him for the sin he afterward endured. God blots out the offense, but does not leave it unpunished. For either man punishes himself in repentance, or God strikes, avenging these things with man. The sin is not therefore spared, because it is not loosed without vengeance. So David deserved to hear after confession, 'The Lord has taken away your sin,' and yet afterward, afflicted with many torments, fleeing, he paid off the guilt of the fault he had perpetrated. So we are absolved by the water of salvation from the fault of the first parent, but though absolved we still die carnally, because God cuts away our faults either through us or through himself even when he releases them. For he strives to wipe away from his elect by temporal affliction the stains of iniquities which he does not wish to see in them for ever.
12.27: 12.27 And Joab sent messengers, etc. RABANUS. This victory of David which Joab began, etc., up to and in the Gospel it is said, that many shall come from the east and west and sit down with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven (Matthew 8). City of waters, etc. On account of the abundance of water that was there, or, as some say, of peoples.
12.30: 12.30 And he took, etc. RABANUS. In Chronicles it is read thus: 'David took the crown of Milcom from his head, and found in it a talent weight of gold and most precious stones. And he made himself a diadem from it' (1 Chronicles 20). For Milcom is not a proper name but is interpreted 'their king.' Milcom, as the Hebrews hold, is the idol of the Ammonites, whose diadem's gold and gems David is said to have melted and purified according to the law, and made himself a diadem.
13.6: 13.6 Little broths. That which is fit for sipping.
13.14: 13.14 He oppressed her. RABANUS. The incest of Amnon, David's eldest son, with his sister Tamar, and the parricide of Absalom against his brother Amnon, admonishes us to act always cautiously, lest vices rule in us; and lest the prince of sin, who promises a false peace to those in peril, finding us unprepared, slay us unawares. For Absalom is interpreted 'father of peace' or 'peace of the father,' Amnon 'giving,' Tamar 'bitterness.' He who gives his members to lust, and serves iniquity unto iniquity, falls into the bitterness of sin, though the enemy shows himself as it were a father of peace and promises prosperity for such deeds. It is necessary, then, that we return quickly to penance, lest perhaps the devil through malignant spirits conspire to our death and hand us over to perpetual death.
13.15: 13.15 And he hated her, etc. Let us too hate the crime committed more than we had loved it before the perpetration, and for this reason we shall sooner obtain pardon, if only we do not offend anew in another vice as Amnon did: who, because after the incest he did not avoid drunkenness, on this account did not escape death.
13.37: 13.37 Talmai. This was the father of Maacah, the mother of Absalom, whom the Hebrews say David took in battle, and, her hair and nails cut according to the law, took her as his wife, and had by her Tamar and Absalom.
13.39: 13.39 And the king ceased. In the Hebrew, the king ceased to go out after Absalom. For David is reported to have wished to go out after Absalom to call him back, but thinking that as often as he saw him he would bring to memory the death of Amnon, he ceased to go out.
14.6: 14.6 And your handmaid, etc. JEROME. The Hebrews say that this woman truly had two sons and had quarreled over an inheritance and that one was slain by the other; yet the woman put herself in the person of David: and the sons in the person of Amnon and Absalom: and the kinsfolk who rise against the son, in the person of the other sons of David.
14.9: 14.9 On me, my lord. THE SAME. As if she said: since one rose against the other, let the iniquity be on me, if indeed it must be; but on you let there be none, because you are without fault, and as I am without fault if one of my sons was slain by the other, so also you, if Absalom killed Amnon who deserved death.
15.1: 15.1 After this. For two years he remained in Jerusalem and did not see the king, in the third he was brought in before the king, in the fourth he made for himself chariots and horsemen: which done he drove his father from the kingdom. Nor was he cast out of the kingdom on account of the seduction and slaying of the priests, but for adultery and homicide, Nathan having foretold all.
15.7: 15.7 After forty years. JEROME, Questions on Kings, vol. 3. It was the fortieth year since Saul overthrew the city of Nob, etc., up to Isaac and Jacob.
15.24: 15.24 And they set down the ark, etc. That God might be consulted by the priest Abiathar as to where David should go.
15.25: 15.25 Zadok. The just one bears the person of the saints, who at the time of the Lord's passion departed indeed in body, but were not separated in love.
15.32: 15.32 Hushai. The friend of David. Hushai is interpreted 'hastening'; who, returning to Jerusalem, scattered the counsel of Ahithophel; he signifies the disciples of the Lord from among the Jews who were hidden, Nicodemus, Joseph and the like.
16.9: 16.9 What to me? Abishai alone had said: I will go and cut off his head. And David answered Abishai and Joab: What to me? Do you wish to kill him as you killed Abner? Let him alone. GREGORY, Moralia, book XXX, chap. 9. He who, pressed by insults of words, cannot or is not able to preserve the virtue of patience, etc., up to by whose intervention, God judging, the heavier penalty is avoided.
16.13: 16.13 But Shimei. RABANUS. This is Nebat, the father of Jeroboam, according to the Hebrews, who is called the son of Jemini, and in zeal for the house of Saul cursed David. The name of his grandfather was Jemini. Shimei himself was of the tribe of Ephraim, son of Joseph, whence he says to David: 'I am come the first today of all the tribe of Joseph.' But Shimei, as is read above, was of the kindred of Saul. Saul was of Benjamin. In Ezra, Shimei is read as the son of Kish, because he was called both Kish and Gera, his father the son of Jemini, that is, of Benjamin, is read here; but he is said to have come first of the tribe of Joseph, because he dwelt in the tribe of Joseph.
16.15: 16.15 Ahithophel. RABANUS. Interpreted 'ruin of a brother.' Judas, acting for the ruin of Christ, gave counsel to the Jews against Christ; both perished by hanging.
17.10: 17.10 And the strongest. JEROME. In the Hebrew: The strongest himself, whose heart is like a lion, shall melt with fear, understand: this David is not understood as the strongest. Hence: For he knows. ISIDORE, in the Book of Kings. According to allegory it must be considered, etc., up to from whose face Christ fled when he left it and passed to the Gentiles.
17.14: 17.14 Absalom. Others take Absalom as Judas the betrayer, whom Christ endured as though he had not known his thoughts, and shared the banquet with him, in which he commended to the disciples the figure of his body and blood. In the betrayal itself he received a kiss from him; therefore Absalom is called 'peace of peace,' because the father had the peace which that man did not have. Ahithophel. RABANUS. Who, departing from David, etc., up to as Ahithophel perished by hanging in his own house, he who plotted against David's life in another's. For he who digs a pit falls into it. 'And the wicked shall be caught in their own snares' (Proverbs 11; 25). Hushai. THE SAME. The Archite, an old friend of David, etc., up to that they may be converted on the occasion of benefits. THE SAME. As to Jonathan, interpreted 'house of the dove,' and Ahimaaz his brother, decreed to spy out the deed of Absalom and report it to David, fleeing Absalom, etc., up to and men, protected from the persecution of the enemy, are freed.
18.9: 18.9 And it happened that Absalom met the servants of David, riding on a mule. RABANUS. Absalom, fleeing on a mule, was hung by the hair of his head in an oak, etc., up to they pass over into the dispersion of the nations, they themselves lost both the principate and the people.
19.22: 19.22 What to me? David feared that if Shimei were killed, the rest who had similarly offended the king would not want to make him their king.
19.24: 19.24 Unwashed. In the Hebrew, uncared for. For Mephibosheth had made for himself wooden feet, according to the Hebrew, which he used in place of natural ones: for he was lame.
19.29: 19.29 You and Ziba. JEROME, Hebrew Questions on Kings. In the Hebrew: I said, You and Ziba divide the field. Which David, forgetful of the covenant and oath, etc., up to words he brought forth obliquely against the Most High.
19.37: 19.37 But there is. But there is in the Hebrew: Behold your servant. In Hebrew it is read Chime han Chanaan; Chanaan is interpreted 'sighing'; as long as he was with his father he was called sighing: but after he passed to the teaching of David he was called not Chanaan but Chamaan, that is, faithful, etc., up to: Ephraim and Manasseh shall be to me as Reuben and Simeon. Great Moses, therefore, and Joshua his successor assigned to them a double lot.
20.9: 20.9 And he held, etc. To hold the chin with the right hand is as it were to flatter out of kindness. But he puts the left to the sword, who strikes secretly out of malice.
20.19: 20.19 Do you not? RABANUS. This is the speech of the law, in which it is commanded that the children of Israel, entering the land of Canaan, first offer peace, and make tributary those who accept peace, but destroy those who do not accept: therefore the wise woman is said to have exclaimed Do you not. As if: Why do you destroy this city before you offer peace according to the law? Why do you not keep for Israelites the law that was once kept for foreigners?
20.22: 20.22 Who cut off. THE SAME. The return of the people to David after the slaying of Absalom, etc., up to that is, Christ the Son of God he returned
21.1: 21.1 There was. RABANUS. The famine that came in Israel on account of the Gibeonites, etc., up to lest by wickedly suggesting they further corrupt their life.
21.8: 21.8 So the king took two. Who with Doeg the Edomite, while still boys, killed the priests and Gibeonites, namely Armoni and Mephibosheth, sons of Michal the daughter, etc. Whom Michal, the wife of David, who is also called Eglah, adopted among her sons, whom Merab her sister had by the son of Barzillai.
21.18: 21.18 Gob. Which is interpreted 'pit,' because as one is cast into a den of lions, so David put himself against Goliath.
21.19: 21.19 The third. RABANUS. Josephus says of the third battle, etc., up to whether he called him Adeodatus or anyone else is uncertain. The fourth, Goliath is repeated, which David did first in the time of Saul. For in Chronicles it is read that he fought against the Philistines principally only the third time. RABANUS. The four wars of David and his servants, etc., up to hence: 'Vain is the salvation of men. In God we shall do mightily, and he shall bring to nothing those who afflict us' (Psalm 107). Bethlehemites, etc. Because Naomi and Ruth, from whom he was descended, returned to Bethlehem in the time of plenty, and because Ruth is known for bread, that place was called House of Bread. Or because Naomi, returning there with her daughter-in-law, obtained abundance of bread in the house of Boaz.
22.1: 22.1 He spoke, etc. RABANUS. Only the seventeenth psalm is found in the books of Kings, etc., up to and with great exultation the gifts granted by the divinity are praised.
23.1: 23.1 Now these are. JEROME. They are the last, because after the psalter and the other meters he is said to have composed this meter, in which he says: 'David the son of Jesse said: The man said, to whom was appointed the ladder of Christ of the God of Jacob.' RABANUS. Because they signify the last praise of confession, which the saints, the enemy overcome and the victory of death completed, will sing for ever. Excellent. Because most brilliantly he prophesied of the Christ of God and of his incarnation and of the redemption of the human race.
23.3: 23.3 In the fear. He who in the fear of God exercises dominion over his subjects brings forth works of light illumined by the sun of justice, and nothing obscure remains in them, but, watered by the rain of heavenly grace, living in the flesh he bears fruit of the shoots of virtues.
23.5: 23.5 Nor is. RABANUS. He who meditates on the law of the Lord day and night becomes like a tree planted by the waters which gives its fruit in its season, and whatever he does shall prosper.
23.7: 23.7 And if anyone. Namely, one who, sharing in others' sins because of the hardness of his heart, is pressed by the weight of iniquities and pierced by the darts of sins, and his works, worthy of eternal fires, shall be reduced to nothing.
23.8: 23.8 These are the names. ISIDORE. A catalog of valiant men is woven in the figure of the saints, who, however much they advance in loftiness of virtues, yet do not reach to the excellence of the divine Trinity. For this is what is written: 'He did not attain to the first three.' For who in the clouds shall be equal to the Lord among the sons of God? Of the valiant. Of these valiant men Josephus says: The first of all was Eusebius son of Ahimaaz, who, frequently breaking through the enemy line, did not cease until he had killed nine hundred. After him was Eleazar the son of Dodo, who had been with the king at Sarpha. When the Israelites were afraid of the army of the Philistines and fleeing, he alone stood firm and slew many, so that the sword clung to his right hand by the blood of the slain. The Israelites, seeing the Palestinians turned to flight, coming down from the mountains pursued them, and a famous victory came to the Israelites. The third was Shammah son of Helez, who, in the place of the jawbone, when the Hebrews fled, alone bore the army of the Palestinians, laying some low, turning others to flight. Himself. RABANUS. The rod from the root of Jesse brought forth a flower without nuptial work, who, from one man bearing the type of the nations, at one stroke, that is by the command of his word, expelled the legion of demons. Most tender of the wood. THE SAME. The warlike and modest strength of the man is signified, etc., up to the strength in the slaying of eight hundred.
23.11: 23.11 Shammah the son. Hearing. Age of, etc. Meditating or speaking. Of Harar. A mountain man, who bears the person of Christ or of his preachers.
23.12: 23.12 He stood. RABANUS. Christ with the Holy Spirit, standing in the field of the Church, protects the weak like barley, or at least defends with the sword of the mouth against lust the modesty of chastity in the incontinent as it were gleaning.
23.13: 23.13 The three had gone down. The three valiant men named above, and Jeshobeam the son of Hachmoni, whom Josephus names Eusebius son of Ahimaaz. And Eleazar the son of Ahohi, whom he says is the son of Dodo, and Shammah the son of Agee, whom he calls Shemaiah son of Heli. The Hebrews, however, think these three were Abishai the son of Zeruiah, and Sibbechai the Hushathite, and Jonathan the son of Shimeah, David's brother, who are mentioned above in the battles of the Philistines. With which opinion what follows seems to agree: Abishai also, brother of Joab, son of Zeruiah, etc. For from this it appears that Abishai was a chief and named among the three that follow. GREGORY. It must be considered that he who has committed unlawful things should abstain also from some lawful ones, that by this he may satisfy his maker, that he who committed forbidden things may cut off for himself even things permitted, and reprove himself in the least things who remembers having sinned in the greatest. The law of the Old Testament forbids coveting another's wife: but that strong soldiers be commanded by a king, or desire water, it does not forbid under penalty. David coveted and took another's wife, and his fault was followed by worthy scourges, and the evil he committed he corrected by laments of repentance. Who, long afterward, sat against the wedges of the enemies, desired water from their cistern; and his chosen soldiers, breaking through the troops of the enemies, brought, unharmed, the water he had desired. But the man, taught by scourges, at once reproved himself for having desired water at the risk of the soldiers, and poured it out as a libation to the Lord. For the water poured out was turned into a sacrifice of the Lord, because he offered up the fault of concupiscence through the repentance of his self-reproof. He who did not fear to covet another's wife afterward feared also because he had coveted water.
23.16: 23.16 But he poured it out. He gave an example of fortitude and constancy to the soldiers, overcoming nature so as not to drink though thirsty, that the army might learn to endure thirst. Mystically, however, he did not thirst for water but foresaw Christ to be born in Bethlehem of a virgin: whose washing and blood he thirsted for. He did not therefore drink the water but poured it out. For he thirsted for the eternal fountain, which is not sought by others' dangers but washes away others' dangers.
23.19: 23.19 The first three. They wish wisdom, humility and fortitude to be understood; for David sat most wise: himself the little worm of the wood, that is, humble, he slew eight hundred as a strong man; to these three virtues none of David's valiant men attained.
23.20: 23.20 And Benaiah. Who was a master of Kabzeel, that is, of the congregation of God among the Cherethites and Pelethites, who are interpreted 'killing and giving life.' He himself struck those whom Chronicles names two Ariels of Moab. These were therefore most valiant men in the kingdom of Moab, whence they are also called lions. For Ariel is interpreted 'lion of God.' In the midst. Josephus here says more plainly what it was, namely, a cistern very deep, in winter time leveled with a heap of snow. Into this a lion unknowingly fell, and shut in, cried out with a great roar. Benaiah, who came with the others to the spectacle, leaped down into the cistern and killed the lion. Benaiah, who is interpreted 'the Lord builds,' signifies Christ, who builds the Church. Whence Paul: 'You are God's building.' He, in a time of snow and cold, namely when the grace of Christ shone upon the world and the chill of charity had made men cold, killed the lion, that is, the devil. The Hebrew understands this lion as Moab, who was slain in the midst of the cistern, that is, in the house of the Lord, where he held the horns of the altar. The altar is called a cistern, because as the water of a cistern washes and cleanses, so the sanctuary of the Lord purges sins. In the days of snow, because through death he expiated sin. Whence: 'You shall wash me,' which was fulfilled in the midst of the cistern; 'and I shall be made whiter than snow,' which was fulfilled in what he said, in the days of snow.
23.21: 23.21 An Egyptian man. An imitator, namely, of the Egyptian blaspheming God, whom Moses killed at the Lord's command; for that one blasphemed God, this one the prophet and king. Worthy. He was watched, that if he went out of Jerusalem he would be killed. Spear. The law of God, which if he had meditated by remaining in Jerusalem he would not have perished, but because he despised the king's command, Benaiah came down to him with a rod, that is, in the rectitude of justice, and wrested away the spear, which he did not hold rightly.
23.23: 23.23 Who were. It had troubled no one that in the sum not thirty but thirty-seven are read. Thirty and seven are read in this way. Seven, namely, these valiant men: David, who is called Adeodatus, Abishai, Sibbechai, Jonathan, Eleazar, Shammah the son of Agee of Harar, and Benaiah, behold seven. The thirty are these: Asahel, Elhanan and the rest.
23.39: 23.39 Uriah. This one is put last for the sake of what follows: And the wrath of the Lord added, etc. For vengeance had already been done on David and his house, but not on the people who either did not resist David or consented.
24.1: 24.1 GREGORY, Moralia, book XXV, chap. 14. According to the qualities of subjects, etc., up to that, as the deeds of masters displease, so the mind of subjects may not withdraw from reverence for authority. JEROME. It must be noted that in Chronicles it is read: 'A thousand thousand one hundred thousand of Israel, and of Judah forty-seven hundred thousand,' whom it is to be understood Joab numbered, but did not wish to show except as many as are written in the book of Samuel.
24.10: 24.10 And he struck, etc. AMBROSE, On Penance, chap. 9. He subjected himself to a greater punishment that he might be able to call forth clemency. For the rigor of justice is softened, etc., up to and the shaking poured out from heaven upon the people ceased.
24.11: 24.11 The word of the Lord. RABANUS. In Exodus it is written, etc., up to seventy thousand were consumed.
24.13: 24.13 Or. And it is seen that those who are not fed with the bread of the word of God through the grace of the sevenfold Spirit endure famine for seven years, and those who are not regenerated in the name of the Trinity are not able to resist enemies, that is, demons; but the unbelieving die by the pestilence of impiety.
24.16: 24.16 And the angel. RABANUS. In Chronicles also it is written: 'And the angel of the Lord stood by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite. And David lifting up his eyes saw the angel of the Lord standing between heaven and earth, with a drawn sword in his hand, turned toward Jerusalem. And both he and the elders, clothed in haircloth, fell on their faces to the ground, by the threshing floor.' The threshing floor of Araunah is the Church of the Gentiles, in which after the true David raised the altar of faith, the death of impiety immediately ceased. David bought this threshing floor for fifty shekels: because Christ, through the grace of the sevenfold Spirit, all offenses being forgiven, sanctified the Gentile world into an everlasting house for himself.
24.18: 24.18 Araunah. THE SAME. Interpreted 'threshing floor': Ornan is 'light for us.' Well, then, David, wishing to appease the Lord, is commanded to set up an altar on the floor of Araunah or Ornan, because God is not otherwise appeased by man unless on the floor of the heart, by the light of right faith and true love, he sets up the altar of humility on which to offer the sacrifice of oblation and praise, whence: 'The sacrifice of praise shall honor me,' etc. (Psalm 49). 'A sacrifice to God is a troubled spirit,' etc. (Psalm 50). The floor of Araunah or Ornan is Jerusalem itself.
24.25: 24.25 And he offered holocausts. Hence in Chronicles the tabernacle which Moses had made in the desert and the altar of holocausts were at that time on the high place of Gibeon, and David could not go to the altar to entreat the Lord. For he had been terrified with exceeding fear, seeing the sword of the angel of the Lord. And David said: This is the house of God, etc. In this place, according to the Hebrews, Abraham wished to offer his son when the ram suddenly appeared: which he took and offered for his son.
